chunks: The insigne Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Muhammad ibn 'Adhafir, from his father. He said: I said to Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him):

Why did God prohibit carrion, blood, pork, and wine? He said: Indeed, God—Blessed and Exalted—did not prohibit these things for His servants, nor did He permit everything else for them, out of desire for what He permitted or asceticism toward what He prohibited. Rather, He—Mighty and Majestic—created creation and knew what would sustain their bodies and what would be beneficial for them, so He permitted that and made it lawful for them; and He knew what would harm them, so He forbade it from them. Then He permitted it for one in dire necessity, at the time when their body cannot be sustained except by it—so He permitted it only to the degree of subsistence and no more than that.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: As for carrion, none who consume it do so without their body weakening, their strength diminishing, and their lineage being cut off; and the consumer of carrion does not die except suddenly. As for blood, its consumption causes yellow dropsy, rabies-like madness, hardening of the heart, and diminishing of compassion and mercy—so one's intimate companion will not be safe from them, nor will anyone who accompanies them.

As for pork, God—Blessed and Exalted—transformed a people into various forms like the pig, the monkey, and the bear, then He prohibited consuming such transformed beings lest one benefit from them or take their punishment lightly. As for wine, He prohibited it due to its effect and its corruption.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: The wine addict is like an idol-worshiper; it causes trembling, it destroys one's manly virtue, and it compels one to dare commit forbidden acts—from the shedding of blood to committing fornication—to the point where, when drunk, one is not to be trusted not to assault his own household while having no comprehension of what he is doing. And wine does not increase its drinker in anything but every kind of evil.

key_terms.الدَّمُ: Blood — flowing blood, prohibited as food in Islamic law
key_terms.الْبُلْغَةُ: Subsistence — the minimum amount needed to sustain life
key_terms.الْمَسْخُ: Divine transformation/metamorphosis — God's punishment of a people by transforming them into animals
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةُ: Carrion — meat from an animal that died without proper slaughter; prohibited in Islamic law
key_terms.الْمُضْطَرُّ: One in dire necessity — the person in a desperate situation where survival requires consuming the forbidden
key_terms.لَحْمُ الْخِنْزِيرِ: Pork — flesh of the pig, absolutely prohibited
key_terms.مُدْمِنُ الْخَمْرِ: Wine addict — one who habitually and persistently drinks wine

ai.seo_question: Why did God prohibit carrion, blood, pork, and wine according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith records a question posed to Imam al-Baqir (AS) about the rationale behind God's prohibition of four substances: carrion, blood, pork, and wine. The Imam explains that God's prohibitions are not arbitrary but rooted in divine wisdom: God knows what sustains and benefits human bodies and what harms them, and legislates accordingly, with exceptions made only for dire necessity. The Imam then details specific physical, spiritual, and social harms caused by each prohibited substance, providing an early Islamic account linking divine law to observable human welfare and social order.
word_analysis: al-Baqir (the one who splits open knowledge)
and made it permissible for them
for the one in dire necessity

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab narrated to us from Muhammad b. Isma`il b. Bazi` from Muhammad b. `Adhafir from his father. He said: I said to Abi Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali al-Baqir (as):

Why did Allah prohibit carrion, blood, pork, and wine? So, he said: Surely, Allah did not prohibit this for His servants, but [rather] He permitted everything else for them out of desire for what was made lawful for them. There is no discipline (zuhd) in what was prohibited for them. Rather, He created the creation, and He knew what would strengthen their bodies and what would rectify them, so He made that lawful and permitted for them; and He knew what would harm them, so He prohibited that from them. Then, he made those things permissible for those in a desperate situation, in which their bodies would not be strengthened except through them. So, He only permitted the quantity sufficient [to stay alive] and not more than that.

Then, he (as) said: As for carrion, none consume it except that it weakens their body, diminishes their strength, and cuts off his offspring. A consumer of carrion does not die except suddenly. As for blood, its consumption causes yellow urine, kidney disease, the hardening of the heart, and the deterioration of kindness and mercy – so their partner and companions will not be safe from them.

As for pork, Allah transfigured a people into different forms in the likeness of swine, monkeys, and bears. Then, He prohibited consuming that likeness so that one may not seek benefit from it or underestimate its punishment. As for wine, its prohibition is due to its affect and its corruption.

Then, he (as) said: Surely, the wine addict is like the worshiper of idols. It causes trembling and it diminishes masculinity. It causes a person to dare to commit unlawful things, from the shedding of blood to adultery – to the point where his female relatives are unsafe from him when he is drunk and not comprehending [what he is doing]. Wine does not increase anything for its drinker except in every evil.
